name: shell-reads-incontainer-token
why: a shell reading the in-container projected token path is Procedure E, the credential read the node sensor must catch
source: synthetic: Linux EDR file_event for TRR9006 Procedure E (head -c 20 of the mounted token); the rule keys on TargetFilename and Image. NOTE: Sigma's linux file_event category is modelled on file creation (Sysmon-for-Linux EID 11); a pure read/open is emitted only by a node sensor configured for file access (auditd PATH, Falco fd.name, Tetragon d_path). Those sensors resolve symlinks, so see the sensor-semantics caveat on the resolved-path cases below

name: node-path-projected-token
why: a read of the token under the node kubelet projected-volume path is the node-side variant; the 'kubernetes.io~projected/' selection must cover it
source: synthetic: EDR file_event for a read on the node under /var/lib/kubelet/pods/.../kubernetes.io~projected/

name: node-path-resolved-timestamp-token
why: 'token' in a projected volume is a symlink to ..data/token -> ..<ts>/token (AtomicWriter), so a d_path/realpath-based sensor reports the resolved ..<ts>/token path. It still sits under 'kubernetes.io~projected/' and ends in '/token', so the node selection catches the resolved spelling too
source: synthetic: EDR file_event with the symlink-resolved node path (kubelet AtomicWriter timestamp dir ..2026_10_12_13_00_00.123456789)

name: kubelet-writes-projected-token
why: the kubelet is the only process that legitimately writes the projected token on the node: its AtomicWriter creates .../kubernetes.io~projected/<vol>/..<ts>/token. The write matches the selection ('kubernetes.io~projected/') and the Image allowlist (endswith /kubelet) alone must suppress it
source: recorded via source: kubernetes pkg/volume/util/atomic_writer.go writePayloadToDir os.WriteFile into the ..<ts> timestamp dir; Image /usr/bin/kubelet, EventType create

name: reads-ca-crt-not-token
why: reading ca.crt in the same serviceaccount directory does not fire: it shares the directory but not the token path. The rule has a single selection item (the token path), so a non-token read shares no positive item with the rule and is a benign sanity floor, not a near-miss (there is no second selection to keep while breaking the path)
source: synthetic: a read of the sibling ca.crt file, not the token

name: kubelet-reads-hostname
why: the kubelet reading an unrelated file (/etc/hostname) cannot fire even if the path matched, because its Image is in the expected-reader filter: a sanity floor that stays quiet

name: run-secrets-spelling-known-miss
why: /var/run is a symlink to /run in most images, so a sensor that reports the resolved path records /run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token; the in-container selection matches any .../secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/.../token path, so this spelling fires (formerly a KNOWN MISS labelled benign)
source: synthetic: the shape of shell-reads-incontainer-token with the /run spelling of the same file

name: incontainer-resolved-timestamp-token-known-miss
why: the projected 'token' is a symlink into the AtomicWriter timestamp directory, so a sensor that resolves links records .../serviceaccount/..<timestamp>/token inside the container; the in-container selection keys on the serviceaccount directory and the token file name, so the resolved path fires (formerly a KNOWN MISS labelled benign)
source: synthetic: the shape of node-path-resolved-timestamp-token, read inside the container

name: binary-named-mount-reads-token
why: a binary named mount that reads the token fires: the mount helper only mounts the volume and never opens the token, so the old `/mount` and `/umount` filter entries only let such a binary read it unseen
source: synthetic: open of the in-container token by /tmp/mount

name: binary-named-kubelet-reads-token
why: a binary named kubelet outside the kubelet's install path that reads the token fires: the filter now pins the kubelet by its full path, not by the image's last path element
source: synthetic: open of the node-side projected token by /tmp/x/kubelet

name: projected-configmap-file-read
why: python3 reading a configMap file from a projected volume shares the kubernetes.io~projected/ directory but is not the service-account token; the old rule fired on any projected file, so the token file name must be required
source: synthetic: open of a projected configMap key on the node; projected volume layout from kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/projected-volumes

name: reads-namespace-file-not-token
why: reading the namespace file in the serviceaccount directory shares the directory but is not the token; flipping only the file-name item fires, so the in-container selection needs the token file name
source: synthetic: open of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/namespace (the projected kube-api-access volume holds token, ca.crt and namespace)

name: node-sensor-marked-reader-reads-token
why: TRR9006 Procedure E reads the projected service-account token off the node through a marked copy of cat (/usr/local/bin/trr9006-reader); the node file-event sensor records the open and the apiserver validator's file-source gate (9006 E) matches it. It is the live-CI event the gate keys on, and it carries the emulation identity so the rename test shows the rule keys on the token path, not on the marked reader's name
source: recorded via source: atomics/T1552.007/src/emulate.sh Procedure E reads the node token through /usr/local/bin/trr9006-reader; auditd -F path=/proc/<node pid>/root<resolved token file> -F perm=r records the open (shape checked on a model node: a private mount namespace and root, the token on a tmpfs mounted inside it); detections/k8s/auditd_file_events.py maps exe->Image, the PATH name->TargetFilename (the path the reader opened, as the node sees it), nametype NORMAL->EventType open
